headline: Public hearings on planBTV New North End and SECORD Phase 1 housing infrastructure, plus a $40,000 celebration grant.
summary: A housing infrastructure agreement with Watershed A, LLC is up for a vote. A request to keep a driveway and curb cut at 15 Ward Street is also on the list, along with work sessions and a closed-door session on problem properties.
items: Consent agenda of 21 items, including a $50,000 state grant for pavement markings, a $1,470,800 SS4A Main Street Signals budget, and tobacco license renewals
Presentation on Winooski Valley Park District's FY26 annual report and FY28 funding request
Public hearing on planBTV: New North End
Public hearing on SECORD Phase 1 Community and Housing Infrastructure Program application
Resolution approving a housing infrastructure agreement with Watershed A, LLC
Resolution supporting graduate student workers at the University of Vermont
15 Ward Street driveway apron and curb cut license agreement, with an option to deny
Work session on Burlington legislative priorities
Work session on problem properties update
Executive session on problem properties and tax liabilities

Recommended Action Following the public hearing, move to adopt the attached resolution adopting the 
SECORD Phase 1 Housing Development Plan; creating the Housing Development Site; 
approving the Housing Infrastructure Project and financing plan; approving the Housing 
Infrastructure Agreement and authorizing the Mayor to execute it, subject to City 
Attorney review; dedicating 90% of municipal tax increment and requesting retention of 
85% of education tax increment for eligible costs for up to 20 years, subject to VEPC 
approval and the Agreement’s repayment provisions; and authorizing submission of the 
CHIP application to VEPC. Substantial changes shall require further Council approval at a 
properly warned hearing and VEPC approval where required.

Recommended Action Motion 1: Move that the Council find that premature general public knowledge of 
pending or probable civil litigation or prosecution to which the City is or may be a party 
would clearly place the City at a substantial disadvantage; 
Motion 2: Based upon that finding, move that the Council and representatives from the 
Department of Finance and Administration, the Department of Permitting and 
Inspection, the City Attorney’s Office, and the Mayor’s Office, enter Executive Session 
pursuant to: 
1 VSA 313(a)(1)(F) to receive confidential attorney client communications for the 
purpose of providing professional legal services to the body; and  
1 VSA 313 (a)(1)(E) to discuss pending or probable civil litigation or a prosecution, to 
which the City is or may be a party.
